record.paper_title: SYMMETRY AND COLORINGS: SOME RESULTS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
record.original_question: Let ms([0, 1], r) be the least upper bound of ε > 0 such that every measurable r-coloring of [0, 1] contains a monochromatic symmetric subset of Lebesgue measure at least ε. Determine the exact value of ms([0, 1], r), at least in the case r = 2.

evidence.quote: this limit is equal to the invariant ms([0, 1], r) defined as the least upper bound of ε > 0 such that for every measurable r-coloring of [0 , 1] there exists a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ [0, 1] of Lebesgue measure λ(A) ≥ ε.
8.3. Problem. Calculate the value ms([0, 1], r) (at least for r = 2).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a Lebesgue measurable subset A ⊂ [0,1], call A symmetric if there exists a point c ∈ ℝ such that A = 2c − A (i.e., A is invariant under the reflection x ↦ 2c − x). A measurable r-coloring of [0,1] is a partition [0,1] = C_1 ∪ C_2 ∪ ⋯ ∪ C_r into r pairwise disjoint Lebesgue measurable sets. Define
   ms([0,1], r) := sup { ε > 0 : for every measurable r-coloring (C_1,…,C_r) of [0,1] there exist an index i and a symmetric measurable set A ⊂ C_i with Lebesgue measure λ(A) ≥ ε }.
Determine the exact value of the invariant ms([0,1], r). In particular, compute ms([0,1], 2).
artifact.status_search_result: The exact value of ms([0,1], r) — including the case r = 2 — appears to remain open. Banakh, Verbitsky and Vorobets ("A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry", Electron. J. Combin., 2000) and subsequent work established bounds and related extremal results, but no closed-form expression for ms([0,1], 2) has been found in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Banakh, Verbitsky, Vorobets establish bounds on the invariant measuring largest monochromatic symmetric subsets in measurable colorings of [0,1].
status_evidence.claim: Bounds known but exact value of ms([0,1], r) not determined.

status_evidence.title: Monochrome symmetric subsets of colored groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies analogous invariants in groups; related work continues to investigate ms-type invariants.
status_evidence.claim: Related invariants studied; exact ms([0,1], r) remains an open problem in the literature.
